fixes.explanation: True, baker. Genesis 38:27 says that when the time came for Tamar to give birth, there were twins in her womb. Twins would mean double the cookie cutters for me, and I'd lose count by the second one. And the next verses have a hand in them.

Canaanite is right. Judah, one of Jacob's sons (Genesis 35:23), leaves his brothers and settles near Hirah, an Adullamite. There he sees the daughter of a Canaanite man named Shua and takes her as his wife (Genesis 38:2). Friend, that verse moves faster than I do when the oven timer goes off.

I see why that one tempts, baker. Verse 9 says Onan knew the offspring would not belong to him. But Judah's instruction in verse 8 is to raise up offspring for his brother. So the offspring would be Er's, not Onan's.

Tamar's father isn't part of Judah's instruction. Judah tells Onan to sleep with his brother's wife and raise up offspring for his brother. That means the offspring is for Er, the brother who had died. Her father's house only comes up in verse 11, where Tamar goes to live in it.

Not quite, friend. The text says Judah thought, “He may die too, like his brothers.” (Genesis 38:11) So his thought is that Shelah may die, not that Shelah is safe. That thought is what comes with his words to Tamar.

False is right, baker. The text says Judah thought, “He may die too, like his brothers.” (Genesis 38:11) That thought comes with his words to Tamar: live as a widow in her father's house until Shelah grows up. I think that's a worried thought.

False is right. Verse 14 says Shelah had grown up, yet Tamar had not been given to him as a wife. Earlier, Judah told her to live as a widow until Shelah grew up (Genesis 38:11). Shelah has grown, and she has not been given to him. That's what Tamar sees.

A mask would sure turn heads on the road, wouldn't it? Genesis 38:14 says she covered her face with a veil to disguise herself. Veil is the word, friend. My disguise would be a mustache, and that gives me away every single time.

A shepherd's daughter isn't what the text says. Judah sees a woman with her face covered, and he thinks she's a prostitute because she had covered her face (Genesis 38:15). The verse names only that one thing he takes her for.

Ring, robe and sandals would be a whole outfit, friend. But Tamar's ask is different: “Your seal and your cord, and the staff in your hand.” (Genesis 38:18) Those are the three things Judah gives her as the pledge.

Cloak, belt and purse is a whole wardrobe, baker. In Genesis 38:18, Tamar answers, “Your seal and your cord, and the staff in your hand.” Judah gives her those three as his pledge, and then he sleeps with her.

Hirah doesn't find her. Genesis 38:20 says Judah sent him with the young goat to collect the items he had left with the woman, and he could not find her. So Hirah still has the goat, and the items are still with her.
That's their answer. The men of that place say, “No shrine prostitute has been here…” (Genesis 38:21) Hirah goes back to Judah and reports it in verse 22. So he returns without finding her.

Tamar isn't named in what Judah says here. His words are, “Let her keep the items. Otherwise we will become a laughingstock.” (Genesis 38:23) That's the only reason he gives, and it's about being laughed at.
Marrying Shelah isn't what Judah orders. In Genesis 38:24 he says, “Bring her out! Let her be burned to death!” That's a heavy order, friend. Nothing in his words there is about Shelah.

Righteous is it. Judah says, “She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to my son Shelah.” (Genesis 38:26) He names what he did not do. Friend, I'd say owning a mistake out loud is a good example for all of us.

Not quite, baker. The midwife announces, “This one came out first,” while the hand is out. But then the baby pulled his hand back and his brother came out (Genesis 38:29). The one with the scarlet thread around his wrist came out after that (Genesis 38:30).

False is right. The baby pulled his hand back and his brother came out (Genesis 38:29). Then his brother came out with the scarlet thread around his wrist (Genesis 38:30). So the twin with the thread was born second. Friend, I'd have dropped that thread and my mustache would've been no help.
